title: Site profile
description: Defines how the generic scraping engine talks to one retailer site.

search.description: How to run a query and read the result list. The three result selectors are required whatever the product page's extraction layer is, because no search page seen so far carries structured data: the list of hits is always read out of the rendered markup. strategy overrides the site-wide one for this one page, which some sites need when their results are built in the browser but their product pages are not.

request_headers.description: Extra HTTP headers sent with this site's requests, merged over the defaults. The search page can replace the set with its own search.request_headers, which some sites need: one platform's variant endpoint answers 200 with an empty body without X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, and answers that same header on its search page with a 404. One platform's variant endpoint answers 200 with an empty body unless the request carries X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. Do not name User-Agent here: the curl_cffi strategy matches its header set to its TLS fingerprint, and overriding one half desyncs the two.

variant_control.description: The product page's own size picker, as a "<css>::attr(name)" or "<css>::text" selector matching one option each. When present, a page whose picker offers more sizes than the extraction layer produced rows fails loudly instead of contributing a table that is quietly missing sizes. Options that read as empty are ignored, so a leading "choose a size" placeholder does not need excluding. A page the selector does not match at all is not checked: that is a plain full bottle. On a GET endpoint profile this costs one extra request per product, because that layer otherwise never opens the product page.

out_of_stock.description: A plain CSS selector matching markup the shop only writes on a product page it has run out of, such as the "notify me when it's back" button that replaces add-to-cart. Sold-out pages are the one case where a page that reads as unpriceable says nothing about the profile, so naming this keeps two loud failures from firing on stock facts: a POST variant endpoint whose body fields sit on the missing add-to-cart button returns no sizes instead of failing, and a search whose only opened page was sold out reports empty instead of a broken profile. A profile that names nothing keeps the older, stricter behavior.

endpoint.description: The GET form is one request per product: product_json is a per-product URL template ({base_url}, {product_url}) that already answers with every size. The POST form is for a platform whose endpoint takes one size option per request instead: product_json is then the one fixed endpoint URL ({base_url} only), body maps each static form field to the selector that reads its value off the product page (a product id sitting on the add-to-cart button, for instance), option_selector finds every size option's own id on that page, and option_body_key names the form field one of those ids goes in. One request is sent per option found, and their rows are combined.

embedded_json.description: Where on the page a JSON blob hides that carries the variant table. source=script reads a <script> body, optionally scanning forward from marker to the JSON value that follows it; source=attribute reads an attribute value. variants_path locates the variant list or size-keyed object inside that JSON, and is omitted when the document itself is the list. In field_map, the value "@key" means the key a variant sits under rather than a field inside it.
